text:
Pittsburgh arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, fresh off a 5-2 win in Los Angeles that snapped a four-game winless run (0-3-1). They're still 1-3-1 in their last five, and they're without Bryan Rust, Elmer Soderblom and Trevor van Riemsdyk. Tommy Novak has taken Rust's spot beside Crosby and Rakell. Anaheim has won four straight, the latest a 5-3 comeback in Calgary after trailing by two. That run owes a lot to finishing: the Ducks have 21 goals on 12.8 expected over the streak, so we wouldn't treat it as proof they're dominating games.

Pittsburgh has the better underlying numbers. At five on five the Penguins have taken 52% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality), against 45% for the Ducks. Anaheim takes 5.2 penalties a game, though its power play (0.72 expected goals a game) outranks Pittsburgh's (0.44). Neither projected goalie has helped his team: Arturs Silovs sits at -1.5 goals saved above expected (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots called for) this season and -12.8 last year, and Laurent Brossoit is at -1.8 this season and -2.8 in one game last year. Our model leans slightly to Anaheim, 3.42 expected goals to 3.22.

Cutter Gauthier is the name to watch: we have him at 45% to score and 70% for a point, riding a seven-game point streak. Beckett Sennecke plays his 100th NHL game, and Sidney Crosby, drafted first overall in 2005, just moved to sixth all-time in NHL scoring, as Daily Faceoff posted. Our under-the-radar picks: Judd Caulfield, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous lately (24% to score), and Ben Kindel, at 45% for a point.
